content: Tweaking is a colloquial term used to describe an individual who is visibly under the influence of methamphetamine. This term is sometimes used in a derogatory manner. When used as an adjective, a person who is tweaking may also be referred to as being twacked. Chronic users of methamphetamine are often referred to as tweakers, and among users, the drug itself is sometimes called tweak. In severe cases, the effects of methamphetamine use can escalate to full-blown amphetamine psychosis. The term tweaking is most commonly used by the general public to describe someone exhibiting pronounced symptoms of methamphetamine use. These symptoms may include punding, which is the repetitive performance of meaningless tasks, hyperactivity, difficulty engaging in social interactions, loss of appetite, neglect of personal hygiene, exaggerated fidgeting, or formication, which is the false sensation of insects crawling on or under the skin. Among amphetamine users, the term may sometimes refer specifically to the negative effects of the drug, while at other times it may simply describe being under the influence of the drug, regardless of whether the effects are apparent to others. Users often report that the negative effects of methamphetamine use can be mitigated by remembering to eat, drink, and bathe while under the influence. This observation suggests that some of the psychotic symptoms associated with methamphetamine use may be caused by sleep and food deprivation rather than the drug itself. Additionally, the term tweaking may also be used to describe the effects of other stimulants, such as cocaine, amphetamine, methylphenidate, or even caffeine.
